mentions.name: Typegres
mentions.description: Typegres is a type-safe TypeScript data layer for PostgreSQL, positioned as a "translator, not an abstraction" rather than a traditional ORM. It exposes the full power of PostgreSQL — all statements and built-in functions — through a type-safe TypeScript API. Its latest feature is class-based models with methods that are composable SQL expressions, letting tables carry expressive business logic and fully composable relations usable anywhere in a query (SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, etc.).
mentions.problem: ORMs have hidden the power of PostgreSQL behind generic, database-agnostic abstractions that made sense in 2010 but are now a bottleneck for modern TypeScript + PostgreSQL stacks.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm working on Typegres, a new data layer for the modern stack (TypeScript + PostgreSQL).

My take is that for years, ORMs have hidden the power of PostgreSQL behind generic, database-agnostic abstractions. This made sense in 2010, but now it's a bottleneck.

Typegres rejects this. It's a "translator, not an abstraction," designed to express the full power of PostgreSQL (all statements, built-in functions, etc.) in a type-safe TypeScript API.
